title: Photosynthesis
objective: After this level you can explain how plants make sugar from light, water and air.
summary: Van Helmont's willow gained 164 pounds but its soil barely changed. Plants build themselves from carbon dioxide and water, powered by light, and give off oxygen from split water.

cards.headline: A tree is built mostly out of thin air.
cards.body: Not soil. It took centuries to work that out, and the first careful experiment got the answer wrong.

cards.headline: The willow in the pot
cards.body: In the 1600s, Jan Baptista van Helmont planted a 5-pound willow in 200 pounds of soil and gave it only water for five years. The tree grew to 169 pounds. The soil lost about 2 ounces. So 164 pounds of tree had come from somewhere, and it clearly wasn't the dirt. Van Helmont concluded it came from the water alone. He never thought to suspect the air.

cards.fact: Six carbon dioxide + six water + light makes one glucose + six oxygen.
cards.context: That's photosynthesis, powered by light captured by chlorophyll. The glucose's carbon comes straight from carbon dioxide in the air, and that carbon makes up most of what a plant builds itself from. Van Helmont was half right: water is an ingredient. The rest of his willow was, mostly, air.

cards.headline: The oxygen comes from the water
cards.body: Here's a twist: the oxygen a plant gives off doesn't come from the carbon dioxide. It comes from splitting water. In 1941, scientists proved it by tagging the water with a heavier kind of oxygen, oxygen-18, and finding that tag in the oxygen gas given off. So the oxygen a plant releases was once part of a water molecule.

cards.headline: Photosynthesis: traced
learned: Van Helmont's willow gained 164 pounds; the soil barely changed
Carbon dioxide + water + light makes glucose + oxygen
Most of a plant's building material is carbon from the air
The oxygen released comes from splitting water

questions.prompt: From carbon dioxide, water and light, photosynthesis makes _____.

options.label: protein and nitrogen
options.rationale: Photosynthesis makes a sugar, not protein.

options.label: carbon dioxide and salt
options.rationale: Carbon dioxide is an ingredient, not a product.

questions.explanation: Six carbon dioxide and six water molecules, with light, make one glucose and six oxygen molecules.

questions.prompt: Match each part of photosynthesis with where it comes from.

pairs.left: The oxygen a plant gives off

questions.explanation: The glucose's carbon comes from carbon dioxide in the air, the oxygen a plant gives off comes from splitting water, and light is captured by chlorophyll.

questions.prompt: The 1941 test tagged water with oxygen-18. From Level 15, why could that tag stand in for ordinary oxygen?

options.label: Isotopes of an element react almost identically
Oxygen-18 has fewer protons, so it is lighter
options.rationale: It is still oxygen, with the same protons; its extra mass is neutrons.

options.label: Oxygen-18 never takes part in reactions
options.rationale: Then the tag could never turn up in the oxygen gas.

options.label: Plants can't tell water from carbon dioxide
options.rationale: The test worked because it told those two sources apart.

questions.explanation: Isotopes behave almost identically in reactions, so oxygen-18 follows the same path as ordinary oxygen.
